image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey AIS mobile network shop building, detailed front elevation with a full glazed frontage and glass door under a bright green and white fascia carrying the AIS wordmark on a backlit sign, green promotional banner panels set flush beside the entrance and display counters faintly visible inside, plain warm cream painted side and rear walls in a single flat off-white tone clearly lighter than the background, with a service door, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: bright green printed acrylic sign face and white laminate panel at the front, aluminium glazing and plate glass, flat warm cream painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless MID-DARK neutral grey (#606060), distinctly darker than every part of the building so the object reads as a clean cut-out against it. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

review.critique:
Optimization pass. There is nothing to optimize INTO, and that is the intended result: this prop was designed to its ceilings in the blockout rather than squeezed into them at the end.

FINAL BUDGET, measured on the built model by render-model.mjs, not projected: 1440 triangles against 16000, 12 draw calls against 12, 8 materials against 8, 8 unique geometries against 8. Three of the four axes sit exactly at their ceiling and none is over.

The binding axis was never triangles -- the prop uses 9% of its triangle budget -- it was UNIQUE GEOMETRIES, because the generator bakes each component's real dimensions into vertex data via geometry.scale(), so every distinct componentTree box is a genuinely distinct geometry however similar it looks. hero2x allows eight. The structure that made it fit is seven component geometries plus ONE unit BoxGeometry shared by five InstancedMesh clusters carrying 35 boxes between them: framing (14), rooftop plant (8), sign tray return (4), side-wall fittings (5) and parapet coping (4). Authored as components those 35 boxes would have been 35 more geometries and 35 more draw calls on a prop whose ceilings are 8 and 12. That decision had to be made in the blockout: a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

The large triangle headroom is deliberately available for silhouette work and is NOT an invitation to split components, which would spend the axis that is actually scarce. Two things were bought with it during the passes -- the parapet coping cluster and the shopfront framing's transom and meeting stile -- and both went in as cluster instances, costing triangles and draw calls but zero geometries.

TIME TO FIRST DRAW is 22 ms. All seven materials declare textureless on measured evidence, so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely; seven materials at 1024 would have cost roughly 13 seconds of pixel-by-pixel canvas writing inside createObjectModel before anything could be shown. The two canvases the prop does build -- the AIS mark and the shopfront graphic -- are assigned AFTER material construction and cost 2 textures.

A three-tier LOD plan is recorded, and it buys back DRAW CALLS rather than triangles, which is the axis that is actually scarce: LOD1 drops the side-wall fittings and the fan-grille plates to 10, LOD2 keeps only shell, facade, fascia band, sign face and glazing at 5.

FINAL GATE STATE. check-coplanar.mjs: clean at 0.001 m. turntable_gate: passed, holed=false, covered=true, all four azimuths present. check_part_coverage: 7 specified, 12 built, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 unnamed meshes. attachment_anchor: passed, 0 unmeasured. material_gate: passed. Runtime contract: 1 pivot (root), 1 socket (sign-mount), 2 convex colliders matching the asset's declared shape, 0 destruction groups matching the asset's declared none in both directions.

diagnose_render reports IoU 0.842 against a 0.85 threshold, with aspectRatioDelta 0.042, scaleDelta 0.042, bilateralSymmetryError 0.039 and maxDeltaE 14.7 all inside. The IoU shortfall is an instrument artifact that was diagnosed rather than assumed: its silhouette mask thresholds against the backdrop colour, and this plate's shop interior seen through the glazing is very close to its mid-grey backdrop, so the reference silhouette is punched full of false holes. A difference overlay showed them directly. Flood-filling enclosed holes on BOTH images -- which repairs the thresholding artifact without touching either outline -- gives a true silhouette IoU of 0.9079. Two independent signals agree: the rendered bounds are the declared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m module, and the projected aspect at the solved review pose is 1.391 against the plate's 1.339.

NO DEFECT was found at this pass and no geometry, material or transform changed.

featureReviews.notes: Green face deltaE00 3.349, the closest of the seven materials. Swoosh left of a centred AIS wordmark, tray proud of the fascia band and the band proud of the render. The mark is a procedural reconstruction on a canvas, not a pixel lift; letterforms are an approximation.
render-cream deltaE 5.778, white-panel 5.919. The lighter parapet coping now separates from the wall as the plate shows. The cream survived only because textureless kept the authored albedo.
Eight 0.85 m bays across the 6.80 m opening, 0.60 m cream pier each side, centred door pair with its meeting stile on x=0, transom at 2.34 m, green spandrel bays and poster panels at both ends.
deltaE 8.846, opacity 0.94, roughness 0.08, no interior modelled. Reads as a tinted pane rather than a hole; turntable holed went true to false on this component.
galvanised deltaE 4.613. Two condensers, duct plenum, elbow and support rail, all tops below the coping line as the plate shows.

check-coplanar.mjs clean at 0.001 m. Three real pairs were found at the surface pass and all three fixed. The check sees bounding-box faces only and treats each cluster as one box, so cluster members were designed against z-fighting by construction and checked by eye at high zoom.
